query: Why do some incidents take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: open_to_close_days_bucket
per_column.rationale: This bucketed resolution duration is the direct dependent variable for 'why do some incidents take longer to resolve' -- highly useful for grouping. Values are derivable from opened_at/closed_at. However the row samples show a grounding flaw: rows 2-5 have identical sys_updated_on and closed_at timestamps yet are bucketed 'one_to_three_days', while row 1 with the same pattern is 'same_day'. Without opened_at shown the derivation appears inconsistent, lowering groundedness somewhat.

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: A cleaned category (email, vpn, database, network) gives a genuine axis to compare resolution times across incident types. It overlaps partially with the original 'category' column but is derived from short_description and is more granular/text-grounded. Sample values (VPN->vpn, WiFi->network_connectivity, database->database) are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: Failure mode (connection_failure, service_unresponsive, outage) is a strong new axis for explaining resolution duration and not redundant with existing columns. Mostly well grounded: 'Cannot connect'->connection_failure, 'not working properly'->service_unresponsive are reasonable, though some mappings require mild inference and null for silent rows is acceptable.

per_column.name: affected_component
per_column.rationale: Distinguishes server_side / network_infrastructure / client_application, a useful grouping axis for resolution time. Grounding is generally reasonable but some inferences are aggressive, e.g. 'Email system not working' -> client_application is a debatable read (could be server_side), indicating warranted-but-uncertain inference rather than direct extraction.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Scope (system_wide, department_wide, individual_user) is a plausible driver of longer resolution and a good analytical axis. But some values are not well supported: 'Cannot connect to database' -> individual_user and 'Email system not working properly' -> system_wide assert scope the terse text does not state, indicating some invented specifics.

per_column.name: assigned_at_open
per_column.rationale: A boolean for whether the incident was assigned at open time is a reasonable explanatory factor for delays. It is near-binary skewed (435 true) reducing leverage somewhat, and its derivation from the shown fields is not clearly demonstrated in the samples, giving moderate groundedness.

per_column.name: resolver_match
per_column.rationale: Whether assigned_to matches closed_by is a plausible workflow signal that could relate to resolution time. Derivable from original columns, so it is somewhat mechanical but adds a comparison axis. Moderate usefulness; derivation is sound where those fields exist, null where not.

per_column.name: assignee_id
per_column.rationale: This is essentially a normalized restatement of the existing 'assigned_to' column, so it is largely redundant, though a clean assignee axis with an explicit 'unassigned' value can help compare resolution times by resolver. Values are grounded in the original assignment fields.

per_column.name: caller_id_group
per_column.rationale: Appears to be a near-restatement of the original caller_id (individual caller names, not a meaningful grouping despite the name). It adds little analytical leverage beyond the existing column for explaining resolution duration. Values are grounded in caller_id.

judge.rationale: The added set provides the key dependent variable (resolution-time bucket) plus several genuinely useful explanatory axes (incident_category, failure_mode, affected_component, scope_indicator) that let the analyst group and compare why some incidents resolve slower. A few columns are redundant restatements of originals (assignee_id, caller_id_group) or skewed near-constants (assigned_at_open), lowering holistic usefulness. Groundedness is generally solid for extraction-style columns, but text-inference columns (scope_indicator, affected_component, and inconsistent duration bucketing in the samples) occasionally assert specifics the terse short_descriptions do not clearly support, warranting a moderate deduction.
